title: Jordan Operational Update - February-March 2026
content: OPERATIONAL CONTEXT In February, Barham Salih undertook his first official visit to Jordan as the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees. During the visit, he reaffirmed UNHCR’s commitment to working with the Government, donors, and partners to support refugees and host communities, and to advance long‑term solutions. The High Commissioner emphasized that a significant number of refugees are expected to remain in Jordan for the foreseeable future, with many becoming increasingly vulnerable. In March, UNHCR closed its field office in Irbid after 12 years of serving refugees in northern Jordan. UNHCR maintains presence in the north through a newly established Irbid Field Unit which will continue to provide services to refugees with support from the UNHCR Country Office in Amman.

The challenge of adapting to a new environment, coupled with the uncertainty of their future, may become overwhelming. Furthermore, refugees often face cultural, linguistic, and social barriers in their new environments. Responding directly to their queries and helping them navigate the laws and regulations in a language they understand reduces their anxiety and reliance on unverified sources of information. Communication with Communities (CwC) is a core element of UNHCR’s protection response and operational priority in Türkiye. title: UNHCR Higher education for rebuilding lives in Türki̇ye - April 2026
content: Context Refugees' access to higher education plays a pivotal role in sustainable development. It directly contributes to the self-reliance, protection environment, resilience and economic prospects of refugees and their communities. Education empowers young refugees to become agents of change, promoting social cohesion and contributing to more stable and prosperous societies. Refugees with higher education are more likely to contribute meaningfully to the host communities in which they live or to the economic and social reconstruction of their home countries when they can return home. A high rate of refugee students find formal employment following graduation. content: Resettlement Many refugees live in perilous situations or have urgent protection needs that cannot be addressed in the first country of asylum. title: UNFPA Situation Report: Lebanon Crisis (26 March - 1 April 2026)
content: One month into the conflict, the humanitarian situation in Lebanon remains critical. Escalating hostilities, restricted access, and continued attacks on civilian and health infrastructure are driving urgent needs. title: UNHCR Iraq Monthly Update February 2026
content: CONTEXT As of the end of February 2026, Iraq generously hosts over 351,000 refugees and asylum-seekers, the majority (88%) of whom are Syrians. Close to 81% of this population resides in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. While most refugees and asylum-seekers live in urban and peri-urban settings, 26% remain in nine refugee camps across the country. Additionally, some 101,700 Internally Displaced People (IDPs) live in 18 IDP camps. UNHCR works with the Government of Iraq and partners to support the access of refugees and asylum-seekers to protection and their inclusion in public services, such as education and healthcare, as well as their access to economic opportunities and in advancing solutions.
